test.title: Checking your bicycle
textTitles: Checking your bicycle before a ride

texts.title: Checking your bicycle before a ride

paragraphs.text: Before every ride, it is worth checking a few parts of your bicycle. Start with the tyres: press them with your thumb, and if they feel soft, pump them up to the pressure printed on the side.
Next, check the brakes. Squeeze each brake lever on the handlebars and make sure the brake pads touch the wheel rim evenly and firmly.
Look at the chain. It should be clean and lightly oiled; a dry or rusty chain makes pedalling harder and wears out faster.
Finally, adjust the saddle so that your leg is almost straight when the pedal is at its lowest point, and make sure the front and rear lights work if you ride after dark.

If you find a problem you cannot fix yourself, most bike shops offer a quick safety check, and some community workshops will show you how to do simple repairs. It is also a good idea to carry a small pump.
